text.p: Following are highlights of some of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- New U.N. Transitional Administrator William Walker begins his mandate in Vukovar.
- INA oil company's general manager Davor Stern says there will be no petrol price changes until September, when prices could either drop or increase.
- Bosnian Serb special police units loyal to Biljana Plavsic end the siege of the Banja Luka police station, while Plavsic announces early elections.
- Clashes among the top officials of the Social-Democratic Party, Zdravko Tomac and Antun Vujic, are harming the strongest opposition party in Croatia.
- Two years since the Croatian army military operation "Storm", Knin becomes a city full of life.

- The central statistics bureau tourism figures released for the first six months of 1997 indicate there were some 6.1 million overnight stays, foreign guests accounting for 73 percent, 44 percent more than during the same time in 1996.
- Heavy tourist traffic into Croatia is not ceasing. Some 200,000 guests have entered Croatia at the Rupe and Pasjak border crossings over the weekend.
- Ministry of Justice statement confirms the capture of Pero Skopljak, an indictee of the Hague Tribunal.
- A four-member Zagreb family has to spend 4,168 kuna per month to cover its daily needs.
- There are indications that Ivana Trump may have interest in buying the Riva Hotel on the island of Rab, built with Czech financing.
- Record car sales in the first seven months of 1997 with nearly 25,000 cars sold.
- Some 47 percent of demobilised Croatian army soliders have some type of war-inflicted disorder that prevents them from taking part in normal everyday life.

- The geneticist should not be the new creators, says member of the European Academy of Arts and Sciences Senate, Zvonimir Separovic, commenting on genetic engineering. -- Zagreb newsroom, 385-1-4557075
